definitions.gloss: sense of values, values, value system
definitions.explanation: One's set of beliefs about what is important in life. Used to describe personal, cultural, or generational perspectives on what matters.

examples.japanese: {価値観|かちかん}が{違|ちが}う。
{古|ふる}い{価値観|かちかん}はもう{通用|つうよう}しない。
examples.english: Old values no longer hold up.

examples.japanese: {世代|せだい}によって{価値観|かちかん}は{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: Values differ greatly depending on the generation.

notes:
Composed of {価値|かち} (value) + {観|かん} (view/perspective). Refers to one's personal belief system about what matters in life — priorities, morals, and what one considers important.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {価値観|かちかん}が{違|ちが}う: to have different values
- {価値観|かちかん}が{合|あ}う: to share the same values
- {価値観|かちかん}が{変|か}わる: values change
- {価値観|かちかん}の{多様化|たようか}: diversification of values
- {価値観|かちかん}を{押|お}し{付|つ}ける: to impose one's values on others

USAGE:
Frequently appears in discussions about relationships ({価値観|かちかん}が{合|あ}う is considered important for marriage), generational differences, and cultural change. A common topic in Japanese media and conversation.

RELATED 〜{観|かん} WORDS:
- {人生観|じんせいかん}: view of life, philosophy of life
- {世界観|せかいかん}: worldview
- {結婚観|けっこんかん}: views on marriage
